info.title: SecurePay cases API
info.description:
The cases an analyst works on: the inbox, assigning, resolving, the account history and the compliance reports. Cases are opened by the consumers from the engine's decisions (only the ones with `opens_case`) and escalated by the alerts task after 4 hours (RN-09).

Send `X-User` with your name on every request that changes a case: it is the actor of the case event.

get.summary: Check that the API and its database are up

example.detail: The cases database is not available.

get.description:
The cases an analyst has to work on. Without `status`, the pending ones: `OPEN` and `ESCALATED` (still open after the 4-hour limit, RN-09). `status` asks for one state (`RESOLVED` too) and `assignee` for one analyst's cases.

Highest `risk_score` first and, with the same risk, the closest to `due_at`. `minutes_left` is the whole minutes until `due_at`, negative once it is overdue, and null for a resolved case. Paginated with `page` and `size` (default 20, at most 100).

schema.description: Only this state. Without it: the pending cases (OPEN and ESCALATED).

get.description: Everything the case stores (the engine's decision, the transaction as it came, the resolution and the evidence key) and its events, oldest first: `CREATED`, `ASSIGNED`, `ESCALATED`, `RESOLVED`, `EVIDENCE_ARCHIVED`.

put.description:
Sets the analyst who owns the case and writes an `ASSIGNED` event with the previous and the new owner (`from` is null the first time), with `X-User` as its actor. Assigning the owner it already has changes nothing and writes no event. An `ESCALATED` case can still be assigned; a `RESOLVED` one cannot (`409`).

`X-User` is required. Returns the case with its events.

schema.description: Who makes the change (1 to 100 characters).

200.description: The case with its new owner and events.

example.detail: X-User must have 1 to 100 characters.

post.summary: Resolve a case with its outcome
post.description:
Closes the case: `FRAUD` sets `final_decision` to `REJECT` and `LEGITIMATE` to `APPROVE`. That is how the held transaction is rejected or released: there is no core to call (team decision D4), so the core reads `final_decision` from the case. Stores the outcome, the note, `resolved_at` and `resolved_by` (`X-User`) and writes a `RESOLVED` event, all in one transaction. The outcome feeds the rule precision and false-positive metrics.

Then the evidence is archived for 10 years (RN-12) and its key is `evidence_key`. If archiving fails the case stays resolved, `evidence_key` is null and the alerts task retries it.

An `OPEN` or `ESCALATED` case can be resolved, with or without an owner; a `RESOLVED` one cannot (`409`). `X-User` is required. Returns the case with its events.

parameters.name: x-user

schema.description: Who resolves the case (1 to 100 characters).
schema.title: X-User

parameters.description: Who resolves the case (1 to 100 characters).

200.description: The resolved case with its events.

example.decision_reason: The account received 3 transfers from different senders and withdrew 95% of its balance.
example.resolution_note: The three senders are linked accounts; the customer did not recognise the withdrawal.

data.note: The three senders are linked accounts; the customer did not recognise the withdrawal.

400.description: `X-User` is missing, the id is not a UUID, `outcome` is not FRAUD or LEGITIMATE, or `note` is not 1 to 2000 characters.

example.detail: X-User must have 1 to 100 characters.

404.description: There is no case with that id.

example.detail: Case not found.

409.description: The case is RESOLVED, which is final.

example.detail: The case is resolved; it can no longer change.
The cases database is not available.

get.summary: Report the suspicious operations of a period
get.description:
The compliance cases opened in the period: mule account (RN-03), splitting (RN-05) and restricted list (RN-06), the decisions that open a case. One row per case with its account, `pattern` (the rules that fired, joined by `+`), the amount in the original currency (with its decimals: JPY has none) and in USD, with the rate the engine used (`usd_rate`, `rate_date`; RN-11), its state and its outcome, oldest first.

`from` and `to` are days (`YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC), both inclusive, at most 31 days apart. `format=csv` returns the same rows as a file to download, `suspicious-report-<from>-<to>.csv`, with amounts as decimal text and `usd_rate`, `rate_date` as the last columns. A period without cases is an empty list with `message` (JSON) or only the header (CSV).

parameters.name: format

schema.description: json (default) or csv, a file to download.

parameters.description: json (default) or csv, a file to download.

200.description: The cases of the period, as JSON or as a CSV file.

400.description: A date is missing or not valid, `from` is after `to`, the period has more than 31 days, or `format` is not json or csv.

example.detail: The period can have at most 31 days.
The cases database is not available.

get.summary: List the last 30 days of an account's transactions
get.description:
Every transaction where the account took part in the last `days` days (at most 30, `ACCOUNT_HISTORY_DAYS`), whatever the engine decided: `OUT` when it was the source, `IN` when it was the destination. The amount is in the account's currency (JPY without decimals), with the engine's `amount_usd` and the rate behind it, `usd_rate` and `rate_date` (RN-11, HU-43). `device_id` is only on the main account's row (the source; in a top-up, the destination).

Newest first by `transaction_date`. An account without history is an empty list. Paginated with `page` and `size` (at most 100). The history consumer writes it a moment after the decision, and the alerts task deletes what is older than 30 days.

parameters.name: days

schema.description: Transactions of the last `days` days (1 to 30).
schema.title: Days

parameters.description: Transactions of the last `days` days (1 to 30).

200.description: The account's transactions in the window, newest first.

items.decision_reason: More than 5 outgoing transfers in 10 minutes.

The cases database is not available.

get.summary: List the accounts that shared a device with an account
get.description:
The devices the account used in the last `days` days (at most 30, `ACCOUNT_HISTORY_DAYS`) and the other accounts that used any of them in the same window, read from the account history (`device_id`, only on the main account's row: the source; in a top-up, the destination). It is the network behind the shared device rule (RN-04).

One item per related account and shared device: an account that used two of the devices appears twice. `last_seen` is the related account's last transaction on that device; `open_cases` counts its cases that are `OPEN` or `ESCALATED`. The latest seen first. An account without devices in the window, or without related accounts, is an empty list.

get.description:
One report per listed document of a transaction: when the engine fires `restricted_list`, the cases consumer opens the case and writes a report for every owner of the source or destination account who is on the list. The alerts task e-mails the new ones to compliance every 5 minutes and sets `notified_at`.

Newest first. `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) filter by `matched_at`; a date or time without a time zone is UTC. A period without reports is an empty list. Paginated with `page` and `size` (at most 100).

schema.description: Up to this time (exclusive), by matched_at.

get.description:
What the nightly reconciliation could not match (RN-10: same reference, amount within 0.01, date within 1 day):

- `MISSING_IN_PARTNER` (HU-38): PagoSeguro approved it and the partner's file does not have it. Only PagoSeguro's amount and time.
- `MISSING_IN_PAGOSEGURO` (HU-39): it is in the partner's file and PagoSeguro did not approve it. Only the partner's amount, time and reference.
- `AMOUNT_MISMATCH` (HU-40): same reference, more than 0.01 apart. Both amounts and `amount_difference` = partner − PagoSeguro.

The same reference more than one day apart is missing on both sides (team decision D4). Amounts keep their currency's decimals (JPY: none).

Without `status`, the `PENDING` ones; `type`, `partner` and `from`/`to` (days, inclusive, by `run_day`) narrow them. Oldest `run_day` first, then by partner. `age_days` counts whole days from `run_day` to today in UTC, null once resolved. Paginated with `page` and `size` (default 50, at most 200).

schema.description: Only this type. Without it: every type.

get.summary: Group the pending differences by age (HU-41)
get.description: The `PENDING` differences by age in days (from `run_day` to today in UTC): `0-1`, `2-7` and `8+`. Always the three ranges, in that order, even when one is empty, each with its count by type. `partner` narrows it to one partner.

200.description: The pending differences by age range.

example.detail: The request contains invalid data.
The cases database is not available.

post.description:
Treasury closes a difference with a note (1 to 2000 characters): it becomes `RESOLVED` with `resolved_at`, `resolved_by` (`X-User`) and `resolution_note`, and stops counting as pending. `RESOLVED` is final: running the day again never reopens it, and resolving it again is `409`.

`X-User` is required. Returns the difference.

example.resolution_note: The ATM network rounds COP to whole pesos; adjusted in the partner's next settlement.

400.description: `X-User` is missing, the id is not a UUID, or `note` is not 1 to 2000 characters.

example.detail: X-User must have 1 to 100 characters.

404.description: There is no difference with that id.

example.detail: Difference not found.

409.description: The difference is RESOLVED, which is final.

example.detail: The difference is resolved; it can no longer change.
The cases database is not available.

get.summary: List the reconciliation runs of a period (RN-10)
get.description:
One run per partners' day: the nightly reconciliation reads the four partners' files, matches them with the approved transactions by reference, amount (±0.01) and date (±1 day) and stores the differences. A day run again updates its run.

Oldest day first. `from` and `to` are days (`YYYY-MM-DD`), both inclusive, by `run_day`; without them, every run. A FAILED run says the step and its error in `error`.

schema.description: Up to this day (inclusive), by run_day.

400.description: A day is not valid, or `from` is after `to`.

The cases database is not available.
